questions.q: What does Databricks say about the medallion architecture?

options.t: It is a recommended best practice but not a requirement
It is deprecated in favour of metric views
It applies only to streaming data
It is required for every Databricks table that dashboards read
options.why: Databricks calls it recommended, not required.

questions.explain: Bronze, silver and gold layers improve quality step by step: a recommended best practice but not a requirement.

questions.q: How does Databricks suggest storing fields in bronze?

options.t: As strongly typed columns, cast on arrival so that bad data is rejected early
Mostly as string, VARIANT or binary, so schema surprises don't drop data
Only the fields gold needs
options.why: Bronze keeps the source's raw state.

options.t: As aggregates per hour

questions.explain: Bronze keeps the raw state with minimal validation: most fields as string, VARIANT or binary, plus provenance such as _metadata.file_name.

questions.q: Where should silver be built from?

options.t: From the source system each time
options.why: Bronze is the base for reprocessing.

options.t: Straight from ingestion, skipping bronze to save storage and time
From bronze, mostly with streaming reads of append-only bronze
From gold, to reuse aggregates

questions.explain: Build silver from bronze, not straight from ingestion, mostly with streaming reads; batch reads suit small dimension tables.

questions.q: What does a metric view separate that a standard view doesn't?

options.t: Bronze tables from silver tables, so each layer has its own view
Hot data from cold data
Rows from columns
Measures from the dimensions they are grouped and filtered by

questions.explain: Metric views separate measure definitions from the dimensions used to group, filter and aggregate them; standard views lock their aggregations in at creation.

questions.q: How is a measure read from a metric view?

options.t: `SELECT dim, MEASURE(revenue) FROM mv GROUP BY ALL`
`SELECT dim, SUM(revenue) FROM mv JOIN other ON ...`
options.why: Metric views can't be joined directly at query time.

options.t: `DESCRIBE mv`
`SELECT * FROM mv`

questions.explain: Every measure in a query must use the MEASURE aggregate; columns must be named; join other data through a CTE, not directly.

questions.q: How is a metric view created in SQL?

options.t: `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv AS SELECT ... FROM src GROUP BY ALL`
`CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS LANGUAGE YAML AS $$ ... $$`
`CREATE TABLE ... USING METRICS`
`CREATE FUNCTION ... RETURNS METRICS`

questions.explain: The YAML definition (version, source, dimensions, measures, optional filter and joins) goes in CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS LANGUAGE YAML.

questions.q: A customer dimension must keep the history of each address change. Which SCD type?

options.t: Neither; history needs a separate audit table
Type 1
Type 2
Type 0

questions.explain: AUTO CDC stores SCD type 1 (overwrite, no history) or type 2 (history, for all or chosen columns).

questions.q: A gold aggregate joins orders to a product dimension that changes. Which dataset keeps it correct?

options.t: A streaming table
options.why: Its joins don't recompute when a dimension changes.

options.t: A temporary view
An external table
A materialized view

questions.explain: Materialized views stay correct when sources update; streaming tables' joins don't recompute when a dimension changes.

questions.q: How should clustering keys be chosen?

options.t: The columns most used in filters, up to four; one of two correlated columns is enough
The lowest-cardinality columns
A generated date column rather than its timestamp
Every column used anywhere in queries, so all filters can skip data

questions.explain: Up to four keys, chosen from the columns most used in filters; of two highly correlated columns one is enough; for a generated date, cluster on the original column.

questions.q: What does the gold layer hold?

options.t: Validated, non-aggregated records
Dimensional models and aggregates aligned to business needs
Checkpoint files
Raw source records, kept exactly as they arrived from each system, for audit

questions.explain: Gold holds dimensional models and aggregates for business needs, optimised for dashboards; some organisations keep several gold layers per domain.
